raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AliGraph presents a comprehensive distributed graph neural network platform with distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators, and runtime, achieving significant training speedup and F1 score improvements on large-scale graphs.
differences: AliGraph does not use graph summarization-based mini-batch training
AliGraph does not adopt a leader-worker mode with edge-segmentation graph flow partition
AliGraph does not use attention layer aggregation for returning training results
AliGraph focuses on general GNN platform rather than specifically link prediction

sources.title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
sources.quote: we present a comprehensive graph neural network system, namely AliGraph, which consists of distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to efficiently support not only existing popular GNNs but also a series of in-house developed ones for different scenarios

sources.title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
sources.quote: At training, AliGraph runs 40%-50% faster with the novel caching strategy and demonstrates around 12 times speed up with the improved runtime.

sources.title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
sources.quote: our in-house developed GNN models all showcase their statistically significant superiorities in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency (e.g., 4.12%-17.19% lift by F1 scores)

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Scalability and performance in distributed graph databases
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: This paper presents a comparative analysis of four graph partitioning strategies (Random Vertex, Metis-based, Random Edge, and HDRF) spanning both edge-cut and vertex-cut paradigms for distributed graph databases, evaluating load balancing, communication overhead, and scalability on dynamic power-law networks.
overlaps: Edge-cut partitioning as a method to divide graphs
HDRF is a streaming edge partitioning algorithm
Load balancing and scalability in distributed graph processing
differences: Targets distributed graph databases and OLTP/OLAP query workloads, not specifically distributed GNN training
Compares existing partitioning strategies rather than proposing a new edge-based graph streaming partition algorithm
Does not address subgraph assignment to worker nodes for GNN training

sources.title: Scalability and performance in distributed graph databases
sources.quote: Graph partitioning is a critical enabler of scalability in distributed graph databases, impacting load balancing, communication overhead, and query performance.

sources.title: Scalability and performance in distributed graph databases
sources.quote: four partitioning strategies Random Vertex, Metis-based, Random Edge, and HDRF spanning both edge-cut and vertex-cut paradigms
